stem: Antenatal care (ANC) is best defined as care given to an expectant mother spanning which period?
options: From the onset of labour until delivery
From the time conception is confirmed until the beginning of labour
From delivery until six weeks postpartum

stem: The ideal period for a woman's booking (initial) ANC visit is after the second missed period or approximately which gestational week?
Early booking is emphasized in ANC primarily to enable the midwife to collect baseline recordings, such as BP and Hb, before which event occurs?
options: Much physiological change has started to take place

stem: Early booking is also emphasized because indiscriminate drug use, smoking, or infection can have the most profound effect on the fetus during which period?
options: Towards the end of the first trimester, when fetal organs are almost formed
Only during the second stage of labour
Only in the final week before delivery

stem: Which of the following is explicitly listed as an OBJECTIVE of the booking visit, distinct from simply performing a physical examination?
options: To provide an opportunity for the woman and family to express concerns about the pregnancy
To immediately schedule a caesarean section for all women
To discharge the woman from further antenatal follow-up
To withhold information about the pregnancy from the family

stem: During history taking at booking, information about a woman's age at menarche, frequency, duration, and amount of menstrual flow falls under which history category?
A woman's marital status, occupation, religion, and habits such as smoking or alcohol use are documented under which history category?
Documentation of DM in a first-degree relative, hypertension, or multiple pregnancy in relatives falls under which history category?
The expected date of delivery (EDD) is calculated by adding how much time to the date of the last menstrual period (LMP)?
Gravidity (gravida) refers specifically to which of the following?
options: The number of babies a woman has delivered alive
The number of times a woman has been pregnant, regardless of outcome or number of babies
The number of pregnancies that reached viability only
The number of times a woman has undergone caesarean section

stem: A woman who conceives a single pregnancy that results in triplets is classified, until her next pregnancy, as:
options: Multigravida based on the number of babies
Nulligravida because the pregnancy was multiple

stem: Parity is determined by which factor, according to the standard definition?
options: The number of babies born alive, regardless of gestational age
The number of pregnancies carried to the point of viability, regardless of whether the outcome was live birth or stillbirth
The total number of pregnancies a woman has ever had, including miscarriages before viability
The number of caesarean deliveries only

stem: The point of fetal viability, used to determine parity, is generally considered to be which gestational age or fetal weight?
A woman who has given birth to a single fetus that reached the point of viability is termed a:
A woman who has given birth five times or more is classified as a:
A woman who has never carried a pregnancy to the point of viability, though she may have been pregnant, is termed:
A woman who has never been pregnant at all is correctly termed:
At booking, the general examination of the client is divided into which two components?
options: Psychiatric evaluation and dietary assessment only

stem: During physical examination, assessment of a woman's breast for flat or inverted nipples, discharge, and skin/glandular changes is part of examining which body region?
Abdominal examination during ANC is aimed at assessing all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Fetal size and growth in relation to gestational age
The lie, presentation, and position of the fetus
Deviations from normal such as polyhydramnios or multiple pregnancy

stem: Abdominal examination in ANC comprises which THREE components, performed in sequence?
Before beginning abdominal palpation, which preparatory step regarding the woman's bladder is required?
options: The bladder should be full to aid palpation
Bladder status is irrelevant to palpation
The woman should be catheterized routinely

stem: During abdominal palpation, the midwife should use which part of the hand to palpate, rather than the fingertips?
options: The flat palmar surface of the fingers
The ulnar border of the hand only

stem: Fundal palpation is specifically performed to determine which parameter?
options: The engagement of the fetal head

stem: When measuring fundal height by the finger method during an ASCENDING uterus, how many fingers' breadth represents 2 weeks of gestation?
When measuring fundal height by the finger method during a DESCENDING uterus (late pregnancy), how many fingers' breadth represents 1 week?
When fundal height is measured by tape in centimeters from the symphysis pubis to the fundus, a gestational age of 30 weeks would typically correspond to approximately how many centimeters?
Lateral palpation during abdominal examination is performed specifically to ascertain which fetal parameter?
Pelvic palpation is performed to accomplish which of the following THREE objectives?
options: Determine the fundal height, assess maternal weight gain, and check for oedema
Determine the presentation, identify the lie, and check for engagement of the head in a cephalic presentation
Measure maternal blood pressure, assess urine protein, and check reflexes
Assess fetal heart rate, respiratory rate, and maternal pulse

stem: Auscultation of the fetal heart during ANC is performed using a pinard stethoscope or electronic fetal heart monitor to detect fetal heart beats within which normal range?
A maternal height of over 160 cm at booking is generally considered indicative of:
options: An abnormally large pelvis requiring caesarean section

stem: Reassessment of pelvic adequacy relative to fetal head size typically occurs at approximately which gestational week, when the fetus is almost fully grown?
A pregnant woman is expected to gain approximately how much weight weekly after 20 weeks of gestation, under normal circumstances?
The total normal weight gain expected throughout an uncomplicated pregnancy is approximately:
A sudden, drastic increase in maternal weight, particularly when accompanied by proteinuria and oedema, should raise suspicion for which condition(s)?
options: Normal physiological weight gain requiring no action

stem: A blood pressure reading of what value at the FIRST antenatal visit is considered indicative of hypertension?
On urinalysis during ANC, the presence of protein in the urine, especially when accompanied by increased BP and/or oedema, is suggestive of:

On urinalysis, the presence of glucose is often followed up with repeated random blood sugar testing or a glucose tolerance test to rule out which condition, even though it is commonly due to a low renal threshold in pregnancy?
Ketones may be detected on urinalysis particularly in a woman who is experiencing which symptom?
Bacteriological testing of urine at booking is performed specifically to detect asymptomatic bacteriuria, which if untreated can lead to which later complication?
A Rhesus-negative mother should be followed up to ensure she receives anti-D immunoglobulin within how many hours after delivery?
The blood test performed at booking specifically to screen for sickle cell disease/trait is the:
The blood test performed at booking specifically to screen for syphilis is the:
HIV testing is performed during ANC primarily to know the woman's status and to prevent which specific outcome?
The THREE categories of routine drugs given to pregnant women during ANC are haematinics, anti-malaria drugs, and:
Which of the following is listed as a component of the routine haematinics given during ANC?
The routine daily dose of folic acid given as part of ANC haematinics is:
The current standard regimen for malaria prevention in pregnancy, replacing older weekly chloroquine or daraprim regimens, is called:
The standard drug combination used for IPT in pregnancy is sulphadoxine-pyremethamine, with each single dose made up of how many tablets?
Each single dose of sulphadoxine-pyremethamine (SP) for IPT contains sulphadoxine 500mg combined with how much pyremethamine?
The first dose of SP for IPT in a normal pregnancy is given after how many weeks of gestation?
The second dose of SP is given at what interval after the first dose in a standard (non-HIV) pregnancy?

In a normal pregnancy under the traditional appointment schedule, ANC visits are typically scheduled every 4 weeks until which gestational week?
Following the 4-weekly schedule, ANC visits then become 2-weekly until which gestational week, before becoming weekly until delivery?
During SUBSEQUENT (non-booking) ANC visits, which blood test is routinely repeated?
options: Full genotype re-testing at every visit
Repeat VDRL at every single visit

stem: Focused Antenatal Care (FANC) is best described as:
options: A model requiring the maximum possible number of antenatal visits for every woman
A qualitative, individualised, and evidence-based care model given by skilled providers
A model that only applies to high-risk pregnancies
A purely administrative scheduling system with no clinical basis

stem: Unlike the traditional ANC model, FANC does NOT classify pregnant women into risk categories because:
options: Risk categorization is always accurate and should be trusted completely
Complications can arise at any time in pregnancy, and risk-based prediction is unreliable
All pregnant women are automatically considered high risk under FANC
FANC eliminates the need for any antenatal visits at all

stem: The goals of FANC are represented by the acronym PPDP, standing for Promotion, Prevention, Detection, and:
Under FANC, a minimum of how many antenatal visits is recommended throughout pregnancy?

CASE SCENARIO: A woman presents for her first antenatal visit at 9 weeks gestation, reporting her LMP was exactly 9 weeks ago. Using Naegele's rule, the midwife calculates the EDD by adding to the LMP date:

CASE SCENARIO (continued): This client reports she has been pregnant three times previously: one pregnancy ended in miscarriage at 10 weeks, one resulted in twins delivered at term, and one resulted in a stillbirth at 30 weeks. Including her current pregnancy, her gravidity is:
CASE SCENARIO (continued): Based on the same history, her parity (before the current pregnancy) is:
options: Para 0, since one pregnancy ended before viability
Para 2, counting the twin pregnancy and the stillbirth as pregnancies reaching viability
Para 3, counting all three prior pregnancies equally
Para 1, counting only the live twin birth

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A primigravida at booking has a height of 152 cm. The midwife's most appropriate initial consideration, without yet concluding a diagnosis, is that:
options: This height automatically confirms cephalopelvic disproportion requiring immediate caesarean booking
Short stature may reflect a small-sized family/race or childhood nutritional stunting, warranting attention to pelvic adequacy as pregnancy progresses
Height has no bearing whatsoever on obstetric risk and requires no further consideration
This height is diagnostic of gestational diabetes

stem: CASE SCENARIO (continued): At 36 weeks, the midwife reassesses this client specifically to determine which finding, given her short stature?
options: Whether the fetal head will engage in the pelvic brim without difficulty
Whether she has developed varicose veins

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A woman at 32 weeks gestation has gained 4 kg in the past week, and urinalysis shows +2 protein with mild bilateral ankle oedema. The midwife's PRIORITY concern is:
options: Normal physiological weight gain of pregnancy requiring no action
Simple dietary overindulgence requiring only counselling
A urinary tract infection with no further significance

stem: CASE SCENARIO (continued): Her blood pressure at this visit is recorded as 148/94 mmHg. Combined with the previous findings, the midwife should:
options: Reassure the client that this is a normal finding at 32 weeks and continue routine follow-up only
Recognize this combination of findings as concerning for a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy requiring further evaluation
Advise the client to restrict all fluid intake immediately without further assessment
Discharge the client from further antenatal care

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A Rhesus-negative woman delivers a healthy baby. The midwife's priority action regarding Rh status is to ensure she receives anti-D immunoglobulin within which timeframe?
options: Anti-D is not required if the baby appears healthy

stem: CASE SCENARIO: An HIV-positive pregnant woman is due to begin malaria chemoprevention. Compared to an HIV-negative woman, the midwife anticipates she may receive:
options: Fewer doses of SP than an HIV-negative woman
The same maximum of 2 doses as an HIV-negative woman
Up to 3 doses of SP, more than the standard 2 doses for an HIV-negative woman
No malaria chemoprevention at all due to her HIV status

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A woman at her booking visit asks why her midwife is not scheduling her for ten or more visits, as her friend experienced in another country. The midwife's BEST explanation, based on FANC principles, is that:
options: More visits are always better and her friend's care was superior
Frequent visits do not necessarily improve pregnancy outcome, and FANC emphasizes quality, individualized care over quantity of visits
FANC is only used in under-resourced settings and is inferior care
Four visits are used only to save cost, with no evidence base

stem: The ideal period for booking is after the second missed period or about the ___________ week of gestation.
The expected date of delivery is calculated by adding ___________ calendar months and ___________ days to the last menstrual period.

___________ palpation determines fundal height, ___________ palpation ascertains fetal position, and ___________ palpation determines presentation and engagement.
The normal fetal heart rate range detected on auscultation is ___________ to ___________ beats per minute.
A maternal height over ___________ cm is generally considered indicative of a normal pelvis.
A pregnant woman is expected to gain approximately ___________ kg weekly after 20 weeks, with a total normal weight gain of about ___________ kg across pregnancy.
A blood pressure of ___________/___________ mmHg at the first antenatal visit is considered indicative of hypertension.

Blood tests done at booking include ABO grouping, Rhesus factor, genotype, and ___________ estimation to rule out anaemia.
The VDRL test performed during ANC booking screens for ___________, while the HIV test aims to prevent ___________.
